variants.text: Dubbo is a city of 43,516 people (2021) at the junction of the Newell, Mitchell and Golden highways, about 400 km by road from Sydney, and the largest population centre in the Orana region. Most visitors come for Taronga Western Plains Zoo, which opened in 1977 on 300 ha and uses concealed moats rather than fences. In town, Old Dubbo Gaol, an official gaol from 1859 to 1966, is now a museum. Wellington Caves, 51 km south-east, are the usual day trip.

variants.text: Dubbo sits where the Newell, Mitchell and Golden highways meet in the NSW Central West, about 400 km from Sydney, and with 43,516 residents it is the largest centre in Orana. The draw is Taronga Western Plains Zoo, a 300 ha open-range zoo that opened in 1977 and has a breeding program for rare black rhinos. The city also has Old Dubbo Gaol, a museum in a gaol that held prisoners from 1859 to 1966, and the Royal Flying Doctor Service visitor experience at the airport. Wellington Caves, 51 km away, can be done as a half-day trip.

variants.text: A regional hub of 43,516 people, Dubbo is the largest city in NSW's Orana region and lies at the crossing of three highways, about 400 km west of Sydney. Visitors come mainly for the zoo, where elephants, giraffes and black rhinos live in open enclosures bounded by concealed moats. The old gaol in the centre, open as a museum with guided and self-guided tours, and the limestone caves at Wellington fill out a second day.

tips: No car needed to reach Dubbo: an XPT train runs daily from Sydney, usually arriving 2-3 PM, and the zoo is a 5 km taxi or bus ride from town.
Book zoo tickets online, where an adult is from $51.30 against $57.00 at the gate. The zoo is open every day of the year, with the Zoo Circuit running 9:00 AM-4:00 PM.
Summer highs often pass 40 C, so visit the zoo early or outside summer; Wellington Caves tours run 9:00 AM-4:15 PM and must be booked, so allow a half day with the drive.
